#Pharma is not sick. Pharma is Argan. For those who skipped Molière: Argan is a rich man who has decided he is gravely ill. He is not. He can get out of the chair perfectly well, as everyone around him can see. But illness is comfortable. It is an identity. And best of all, it comes with a whole ecosystem of physicians absolutely delighted to keep him in it. We have been Argan for twenty years. Every few seasons, a new remedy arrives. CRM. Sales Force Effectiveness. Real World Evidence. Digital Marketing. Customer Experience. Omnichannel. Now AI — three times daily, with a steering committee. And guess what? Each remedy works exactly the way a purge works. We feel lighter. We feel that something has happened. Then a new January brings a new budget and the same mistakes. Again... and again .. and again ... Here is the #diagnosis nobody wants written on the chart: we were never ill. We are complacent. We are an industry so profitable that we have never been forced to develop grit — rich enough to survive our own bad decisions, and comfortable enough to mistake activity for progress. If we have a disease, it is one of mindset and culture. And nobody is selling any cure for it. There is no platform for courage. No dashboard for having the difficult conversation while it is still cheap. And we like to believe we are sick, because it allows us to moan and complain, and have many people at our bedside caring for us. In the play, the person who finally tells Argan the truth is Toinette — the maid. In our industry she exists and I hope the room in #Pharmageddon will be full ot Toinettes. I'll be on stage on the 6–7 October in Amsterdam, to argue that we do not need another treatment, we need to get out of the chair and start walking. Bring your Toinette to support me !!! #PharmageddonEU Paul Simms Lucy Osborne Gabriel Pereira De Paula

There are inflection points in our careers that reconnect us to purpose. Last week, I had the privilege of spending time inside the Novartis labs with the scientists who are pushing the boundaries of medicine. Experiencing that environment firsthand reinforces a critical perspective: innovation does not start in the marketplace—it starts in the lab, with relentless scientific commitment. For those of us in and leading marketing and creative functions, this is an important reminder. Our role is not just to deliver campaigns and content—it is to translate complex scientific innovation into meaningful, human impact. When done well, we bridge the gap between discovery and understanding. Between innovation and access. Between science and patients. It is a responsibility—and a privilege—to help bring these breakthroughs to life.

What if real luxury isn’t where you stay, but how you feel while you’re there? This picture isn’t about laundry. It’s about permission to pause. In a world shaped by relentless work pressure, economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and constant connectivity, our minds rarely get a chance to slow down. Even our breaks often come with packed itineraries, notifications, and the pressure to make every moment count. Then there are places where something shifts. A few days in the countryside. Laundry drying between two trees. Fresh air. Silence that isn’t empty but restorative. Time that stretches just enough for your thoughts to settle. These simple moments reconnect us with needs that are deeply human: rest, nature, perspective, and presence. They remind us that recovery isn’t a luxury, it’s a prerequisite for making better decisions, leading well, and sustaining high performance over time. Perhaps that’s the new definition of luxury. Not excess, but balance. Not constant stimulation, but the space to disconnect so we can reconnect with ourselves, with the people around us, and with what truly matters. Sometimes, all it takes is a few days away from the noise to return with a clearer mind and renewed energy. And maybe that’s the most valuable investment we can make.

To stand out in a room full of pixels, we brought texture. At the Alzheimer's Association® this week, we didn't just look to build another high-spec tech footprint. We designed this organic, hanging floral installation to contrast the busy, clinical environment of the exhibition hall. In a space dominated by screens and flashing LEDs, it was this quiet, tactile art piece that attracted attendees and made them slow down to connect. It proves a core belief we hold at mccglc : technology has its place, but genuine human connection is catalyzed by artistic intuition. The most sophisticated way to cut through the digital noise is to introduce something beautifully human. #mccglc #AAIC26 #ExperientialDesign #BrandExperience #CreativeDirection #ArtDirection #Engagement

The future of healthcare innovation is built through partnership. I am proud to see #NovartisUAE and Department of Health Abu Dhabi reach another important milestone in our longstanding collaboration through the signing of an MoU focused on genomics research, scientific capacity building, and advanced therapies during #BIO2026 in San Diego. The agreement reflects a shared commitment to advancing scientific innovation, strengthening research capabilities, and exploring new opportunities that can contribute to better health outcomes for patients in Abu Dhabi and beyond. The Department of Health Abu Dhabi delegation’s visit to the Novartis Biomedical Research site provided an excellent opportunity for meaningful dialogue on the future of genomics and precision medicine, while showcasing the cutting-edge science and innovation that are shaping tomorrow’s healthcare solution. I would like to thank H.E. Dr. Noura AlGhaithi and the Department of Health Abu Dhabi delegation, as well as my Novartis colleagues who represented our organization during this important engagement. I look forward to seeing this collaboration continue to grow in support of Abu Dhabi’s healthcare innovation ambitions. #HealthcareInnovation #Genomics #PercisionMedicine #Partnership #Novartis #LifeSciences #AbuDhabi
